summary: Brush your pet's teeth 2–3 times a week. Use pet-safe toothpaste to stop tartar and gum disease.
detail: Most pets over age three have some dental disease. Start brushing slowly. Use enzyme pet toothpaste — never human toothpaste. Dental chews can help too.

summary: You should feel your pet's ribs, but not see them. Measure meals instead of leaving food out all day.
detail: Being overweight can shorten your pet's life and hurt their joints. Use a measuring cup for every meal. Keep treats under 10% of daily food. Play with your pet for 20–30 minutes each day.

summary: Follow the core vaccine schedule. Keep booster shots on time, as your vet says.
detail: Core vaccines protect against rabies, distemper, and parvovirus. Puppies and kittens need shots every 3–4 weeks until 16 weeks old. After that, they need boosters every one to three years.

summary: Watch for changes in appetite, energy, fur, or bathroom habits. Early signs matter most.
detail: Ear infections, UTIs, and skin allergies are common. They are easy to treat when caught early. Book a check-up once a year — twice a year for older pets.

summary: Always keep fresh water ready. Wet food gives cats extra water too.
detail: Not drinking enough water can hurt the kidneys, especially in cats. Clean water bowls every day. A pet water fountain can help. Watch how much your pet drinks in hot weather.

summary: Use flea, tick, and heartworm prevention all year. Ask your vet what is best for your pet.
detail: Parasites can spread serious disease, even indoors. Use monthly prevention, check stool samples often, and check for ticks after time outside.
